## Build

### 2026-10-02 — October 2nd: Just some basic soldering

**1h**

October 2nd: Just some basic soldering

This was my first time soldering and since I don't have a soldering iron yet at home, I had to borrow one from my school. I was planning to use the standard  parallel twist method in order to splice the wires, but at first it was really hard to get the molten solder to stick to the wires at all. And since my school didn't have any soldering flux there wasn't much I could do about it anyway. In addition to this, the soldering iron tip was extremely oxidised making it kind of annoying to use because I had to wait ages for the iron to heat up the solder. But eventually with some finesse and time, I managed to make some crude solder joints between the wires.

As for the connections themselves, they were really simple. All I had to do was solder the battery holder's positive wire to the fan's positive wire (yellow wire),  and then the 2 ground wires together as well.

![IMG_0411](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/oevoP7jO4uTvd60Ew3652grvpX7eA13X/44bd2266b54dca2f23db725eef4d328cb95e7b5dbc1d03d1c53f041539910002.jpg)

Lastly, I insulated the joints and bundled the wires with some electrical tape, just to make everything a little neater and to avoid any short circuits.

![IMG_0412](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/oevoP7jO4uTvd60Ew3652grvpX7eA13X/5f44d0e6959bf146a247e87f0a1b6c6cf34a92652347de54f7f34c167a0d88ca.jpg)
